root_idea.summary: The supplied lexical tradition presents four distinct branches: gratitude for a benefit, fullness or abundance, fresh growth from a plant, and a euphemistic sexual branch.
root_idea.development: In Quranic usage, the dominant branch is gratitude: recognizing beneficence and showing it through inward acknowledgment, speech, and action. Its intensive adjective can also describe divine recognition and recompense of even small acts. Classical Arabic separately preserves the branches of abundance, emergent growth, and sexual euphemism.

senses.definition: To thank or be grateful to a benefactor for a benefit; to acknowledge beneficence and express it through praise, speech, or appropriate action.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic construction may take لِـ with the benefactor, and gratitude may be directed to God or to people who confer a benefit. The lexical notion is specifically connected with received favor, and may be realized inwardly by recognizing the benefit, verbally by praising the benefactor, or bodily through obedient and responsive action.

senses.definition: One who is grateful or thankful; one who acknowledges and shows appreciation for a received benefit.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participle of شَكَرَ, used for a person characterized by gratitude or for one who is actively expressing it. The form does not by itself specify whether gratitude is expressed in the heart, by speech, or through action.

senses.definition: Intensely or habitually grateful; one who gives abundant thanks and strives fully to show gratitude.
senses.usage_conditions: An intensive adjective for a person whose gratitude is extensive or persistent. The reported modes of gratitude include inward recognition, verbal acknowledgment, and action or obedience; the description may also include gratitude during trial or for what is received only in small measure.

senses.definition: Of God: abundantly appreciative and recompensing, recognizing even small acts of devotion with forgiveness, favor, or multiplied reward.
senses.usage_conditions: A divine epithet describing divine response to servants' worship and good works, rather than human thankfulness toward a benefactor.

senses.definition: Gratitude or thanksgiving for a benefit; recognition of beneficence expressed in the heart, by the tongue, and through action.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction اعْمَلُوا شُكْرًا, the noun can denote performing one's acts as an expression of gratitude, not merely uttering thanks. It is narrower than general praise because it is connected with received favor.

senses.definition: Thanksgiving or gratitude; an act or expression of giving thanks.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun of شَكَرَ. In the classical discussion of the Quranic occurrence at 76:9, شُكُور may be understood either as an infinitive or as a plural form of شُكْر.

senses.definition: Appreciated, thanked, or commended as deserving acknowledgment.
senses.usage_conditions: A passive participle describing the result of being treated with gratitude or praise; the Quranic occurrences present an action or effort as receiving appreciation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become full or abundant, especially of a lactating animal whose udder fills with milk; by extension, to become fat or yield abundant milk after good pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of camels, ewes, goats, udders, and the period or conditions in which milk becomes plentiful. The lexical branch concerns fullness and abundance, not gratitude.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become liberal or generous, giving largely after having been niggardly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from becoming abundant; used of a person who gives more freely after previous withholding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a tree, palm, or vine: to put forth abundant new growth, including shoots, branches, leaves, or bark, or to grow from a planted shoot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of vegetation and its emergent growth; the cited descriptions include palm offsets, branches around a tree, bark, and long or upper shoots of a vine.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tender shoots, sprouts, small leaves, offsets, or other fresh growth arising from a plant's stem or base; also the first fresh herbage after dried growth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun covers soft, new growth of trees, palms, vines, and other plants, including suckers and small leaves beneath larger ones. The Form VIII verb may describe something as becoming such growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Young offspring or young men, including the young of camels, by comparison with tender new growth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application of شَكِير to immature or newly developing beings; the animal and human applications are lexical extensions, not restrictions on the Quranic gratitude senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fine, soft, downy, weak, or newly growing hair or feathers; in particular, hair of the forelock and hair near the face or neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes down on a fetus, hair among plaits, forelocks, and fine growth among coarser hair or feathers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To show another person that one is thankful or grateful to him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III expresses reciprocal or directed display of gratitude and is distinct from the Quran-attested Form I group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To commence discourse with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional Form III expression, شَاكَرْتُهُ الحَدِيثَ, with the object of beginning conversation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of land: to produce fresh herbage after earlier herbage has dried and become dusty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV agricultural usage describing renewed vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To affect or make a show of thankfulness, or to seem or appear thankful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V may describe an outward display or apparent state rather than asserting genuine gratitude.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the sky: to rain heavily or vehemently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VIII weather usage describing abundant rainfall.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of winds: to bring rain or to blow violently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: One reported interpretation describes a contrary wind, but that interpretation is explicitly contested; the secure descriptions are rain-bringing or violent wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of heat or cold: to become intense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VIII usage applied to the severity of temperature.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a person: to strive, exert himself, or do his utmost in running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form VIII usage describing maximal exertion in running.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a fetus: to put forth downy hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare Form VIII developmental usage, explicitly reported as an apparent or inferred application.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The vulva or pudendum of a woman, including its flesh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun, distinct from the verbal noun شُكْر used for gratitude.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sexual intercourse or marriage, used euphemistically.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional euphemistic usage related to the anatomical sense; it is also attested in the expression for the price or hire of prostitution.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A full or abundant spring, source, or eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application of the fullness branch to a source or eye containing much water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fat piece of meat, especially one flowing with grease or gravy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application of abundance or fullness to meat rich in fat or juices.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a beast: one that is satisfied by little fodder and fattens on it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative intensive adjective, explained as though the beast were appreciative of a small benefit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most thankful or grateful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or elative adjective, as in the expression “more grateful than the barūqah plant.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Herbage that causes milk to become copious.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare botanical and pastoral adjective applied to vegetation productive of abundant milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for chicory, succory, or endive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later plant name recorded as an Arabicized or contemporary botanical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hired man, hireling, or servant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An Arabicized word identified as borrowed from Persian; it is not the gratitude branch of the Quranic headword شَاكِر.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular plant, identified in later usage with hemlock or a related species.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The entry records several variant spellings and a Persian connection; the plant has a slender stem and leaves compared with fennel, cucumber, or bryony.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The season or period when livestock have abundant milk or full udders.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional time expression associated with plentiful spring herbage and milk.

cautions: The classical discussion allows شُكُور in 76:9 to be read as either an infinitive or a plural of شُكْر; it is presented publicly as a verbal noun because of its Quranic form grouping and constructional use.

The reported interpretation of مُشْتَكِرَةٌ or اشْتَكَرَتِ الرِّيَاحُ as a contrary wind is explicitly disputed in the supplied lexical evidence; the secure descriptions are rain-bringing or violent wind.
